title: Matched scan crops show a gap on f80r and a readable narrow opening on a dated syringe drawing
statement: Two independent detail readings and then context readings of nine coded crops find a short taper on f80r, fingers overlapping its rounded body, and a visible gap to the same figure’s flank. Known implements in Laud f96r and Arderne X 118 reach a separate figure. Both readers see transverse bands on the Arderne neck. In a supplementary late-medieval instrument drawing, both resolve a front-facing narrow opening across about six native pixels, plus an exposed broad mouth and external collar in a separate crop. The f80r taper is seen in profile and its end face remains unresolved. The reviewed f80r construction and posture leave its identity open.
check: Find at least two independently dated late-medieval pictures of identified handheld objects with exposed working ends, including a medical assembly before contact and a nonmedical rounded object with a short neck if available. Keep the full-source orientation and locate any actual exposed aperture or discrete external shoulder. Freeze feature definitions and crop coordinates before masking. Ask two fresh readers to detect the same feature first at native resolution, then at f80r-scale body breadth and local tip width. Retain disagreements, and score the construction and use pose separately. An unresolvable positive control cannot support an absence claim. A matching preparation pose can keep an identification open, while identification needs both a compatible construction and compatible depicted use.

protocol.summary: Nine grayscale close crops and corresponding context crops. Downsample close crops by box averaging to at most the 43-native-pixel f80r body breadth. Lower-resolution controls retain their native sample count. Integer threefold nearest-neighbor enlargement is for display. Context crops preserve visible figure and tool relationships and are reduced to at most 700 by 620 pixels with Lanczos.
protocol.breadth: Approximate horizontal breadth of the rounded body excluding shaft, projection and stream. The putative Morgan M.165 cup breadth is only approximate because of occlusion.
protocol.order: Two fresh readers coded close crops independently. Both initial results were locked before the context pass. The key and catalogues were withheld throughout. Context readers noted a likely Voynich drawing, so masking cannot be treated as complete source anonymity.
protocol.coding: V is a resolved visible feature. A is an exposed geometric negative at that view. U is unresolved or occluded. An A from a reader does not establish diagnostic absence when no analogous positive feature is resolved. Contacts exclude the gripping fingers. A visible gap is measured relative to the closest illustrated body outline, with intended recipient left open.

definition.rim: a broad opening with visible lip or interior
definition.bore: an exposed narrow-end opening with visible boundary
definition.stop: a discrete external crosswise shoulder distinct from fingers or adjacent lines
definition.bands: transverse wrap or parallel strokes on the neck, recorded separately from a silhouette shoulder

target_trace.coordinate_system: approximate trace landmarks in the native 180 by 130 pixel derivative, x right and y down
target_trace.open_space_across_y90_px: roughly twenty native pixels between the torso contour and projection tip
target_trace.limits: An upper-right section of the object outline is overlapped by the fingers. Strokes are traced separately where exposed. The trace is approximate and not a new optical observation.

H17.use: wide tub, separate from the handheld form at the top of the scene
H17.reading: Both see the outer lip enclosing open interior. About 43 pixels of vessel breadth at comparison scale.

H31.use: external collars on a side-profile photograph
H31.date: Retrieved from the Kronan wreck, which sank in 1676. Manufacture date unspecified.
H31.citation: Lindeke and Ohlson 2018, fig. 5a on printed p. 72
H31.shaft_width_px: about 9 along the thin exposed shaft
H31.reading: Both see external shoulders at the widening rings. Both code the bore unresolved. The source is a photograph with high contrast, centuries later than the manuscript. A manufactured shoulder and a functional stop are separate claims.

H42.use: the V53 bowl at the native 86-pixel breadth
H42.reading: One reader saw a rim and the other found it unresolved. At the 43-pixel exposure both coded it unresolved.

H56.reference: Glasgow University Library, MS Hunter 251 (U.4.9), f43r, England, c.1475–1500
H56.use: lower narrow end of the left detached syringe on the instrument sheet
H56.reading: Both found the narrow terminal mark unresolved despite an exposed tip. No new optical samples were added.

H63.reference: Glasgow University Library, MS Hunter 251 (U.4.9), f43r, England, c.1475–1500
H63.use: upper narrow end of the right detached syringe on the instrument sheet
H63.reading: Both found a separate closed outline bounding a lighter center at the terminal and scored the very small depicted bore visible. That end faces the viewer. No new optical samples were added.

H75.use: wide face and separate collar on the right detached syringe
H75.reading: Both see the broad nested-oval opening and a separate collar interrupting both shaft sides.

other_laud_panels: Direct review of f96v top and bottom confirms repeated ovals at different positions on seated figures with a separate attendant. The middle scene is the coded f96v specimen. These are multiple images from one manuscript and remain one historical source.
limits: Eight external specimen crops came from six manuscripts. The two Laud scenes and the two G.38.II held objects are paired within sources. This is a selected comparison set.
The coarse anatomical placement and visible gap do not fix the drawing’s intended role. A holding or preparation pose remains possible.

Body outlines, hands and applying edges overlap in several controls. The detached Hunter 251 instrument drawing gives a readable bore in one view and an unresolved terminal mark in another. Its angle, line contrast and grips differ from the corresponding details on f80r. The tub and late photograph offer supplementary checks for broad rim and geometric shoulder. A visible wrap and a discrete external shoulder are separate observations.
No external source provides a sufficiently readable independent identification of the target. This experiment assigns no label reading or historical function.
